title: Those Who Face the Gods
html:
After arriving at Veronica Royal Castle, our group rested for an entire day.

Then, first thing the next morning, I got up before everyone else, told the group my plan, and stood at the castle entrance. Lee Hyunsung asked,

“Surely you aren't planning to leave alone?”

“I won't be alone. Those two are coming with me.”

When I pointed at Han Sooyoung and Asuka Ren, Lee Jihye grumbled.

“What are we supposed to do if you just leave like that, ajusshi?”

“You and Hyunsung-ssi will handle the defense (守城) of Veronica. You checked the updated scenario, right?”

“······Protect ‘Veronica Royal Castle’ until the scenario ends?”

“Yes. That's your mission.”

“But······”

“Just do as you're told.”

“······Fine.”

I immediately turned to Lee Hyunsung.

“We have Gong Pildu, but [Armed Fortress] alone will have trouble holding off the incoming disasters. I'm sorry to leave you with all this······”

“Keeping watch in all directions is my specialty, so don't worry.”

His reassuring confidence put me at ease, but I knew it wouldn't be easy. It might look as though I'd given them an easy mission, but in this scenario, staying behind would actually be much harder than coming with me.

“If anyone from the first wave or the ‘snake’ appears, never confront them head-on. You must run, even if it means abandoning Veronica. Can you promise me that?”

“I promise.”

Their mission was to protect this fortress until I returned.

I also made a point of giving Lee Gilyoung and Shin Yoosung firm instructions.

“Gather as many insects and monsters as you can. Your mission is to buy time.”

Lee Gilyoung and Shin Yoosung nodded.

“There are lots of monster species unique to this world in the northern forest. Go there whenever you have time and tame them.”

“Yes, hyung.”

“Okay, ajusshi.”

A large number of monsters would help bridge the gap in fighting strength against the disasters, however slightly. The children's proficiency would probably increase considerably in the process, too.

With that, I left Veronica Royal Castle. Looking back at our companions as they saw us off, Han Sooyoung said,

“So where are we going?”

“The strange rock formations to the east.”

Startled by that, Asuka Ren said,

“Japan has already occupied that area.”

“I know.”

I looked straight at Asuka Ren.

Short hair with a subtle curl. A face with bold, distinct lines, as though a manga artist had drawn it with painstaking care. Her face conveyed something like a warrior's integrity (節槪) rather than mere beauty.

“That's why I brought you.”

“Do you trust me?”

“No. I just want to be repaid for saving your life.”

“······I see.”

Saying it this way would make it easier to win her goodwill. Asuka Ren did, in fact, look as though she was wrestling with something. Once she had finished, she would probably begin telling me what she knew in earnest.

For a while, we made our way toward the rock formations, thoroughly surveying the area around the plains.

The journey was expected to take two days, but we could make it in one if we pushed ourselves.

Han Sooyoung asked,

“So what's the plan?”

“Unlike us, Japan has an [Absolute Throne]. That means there's an ‘Absolute King’ among the first wave who commands them all.”

After thinking my words over, Han Sooyoung said,

“······Don't tell me you're going after the king?”

As expected, Han Sooyoung was quick on the uptake.

I nodded.

“Well······that would solve it. When the owner of an [Absolute Throne] dies, it has a huge effect on the entire group under them······”

“Of course, taking down the king won't kill all of them, but they won't be able to do anything until the scenario ends.”

“Hmm, so you'll take out the boss right at the start and call it a day? I like the ambition.”

That was when Asuka Ren interrupted.

“······You say that, but do you know who Japan's king is now?”

“Isn't it the Sovereign of Eight Heads?”

The Sovereign of Eight Heads. ‘Snake’ for short.

“H-how do you know that······?”

Asuka Ren shuddered in astonishment.

Understandably. As one of the first wave, she would know what sort of being the ‘Sovereign of Eight Heads’ was.

For reference, ‘Sovereign of Eight Heads’ wasn't the Japanese king's nickname, but his sponsor's modifier. He had no nickname because a nickname would be meaningless.

“You seem to have heard the modifier somewhere, but he won't be nearly as easy as you think······”

“I know the true name, too. Yamata no Orochi, isn't it?”

At my words, the sky darkened for a moment, and a rumbling sound rang out.

I wondered whether he might have heard what I'd just said.

A constellation's true name carried that much power.

“······Orochi? Isn't that the name of a monster from Japanese mythology?”

“That's right. He's Japan's king now.”

“Then why refer to him by his sponsor? Doesn't he have a nickname?”

“There's no point. His incarnation isn't in his right mind now. Over the course of six scenarios, he made an absurd contract with the ‘Sovereign of Eight Heads’ and had his soul stolen.”

Asuka Ren's mouth was now hanging open. It must have been shocking to find that an incarnation from another country knew more about her own country's affairs than she did.

“Then he'll be in the rock formations.”

“Yes. But even if we found him right now, we couldn't take him down. We need to prepare for that. We're going to the rock formations because there's someone else I need to meet.”

“Someone you need to meet? What······Yoo Joonghyuk?”

“Someone stronger than Yoo Joonghyuk.”

“······There's someone stronger than him?”

“There is.”

“Who?”

“A powerful fighter from Peace Land.”

Han Sooyoung let out a disbelieving laugh.

“From Peace Land? Are you kidding me?”

I could understand why she would say that.

This information didn't appear before episode 100.

“Don't you know how weak everyone here is?”

Han Sooyoung snapped at me without even giving me a chance to answer.

Whatever had made her so angry, Han Sooyoung was unusually worked up.

“Forget sword masters—there aren't even any third-rate swordsmen here! And all the magic these people can use amounts to lighting a fire in a stove.”

I knew that, too.

“It's not like this is some first-generation fantasy novel······. It's like someone maliciously gathered together nothing but weaklings. No, I just don't get it. Why would those dokkaebi bastards, who love excitement so much, make a world like this their stage? Do they even want to earn coins?”

Listening to her, I began to understand why Han Sooyoung was so worked up.

She might have been a plagiarist, but she was a successful fantasy writer.

“Calm down. The dokkaebis didn't create this setting.”

“What?”

I looked beside me. There stood a woman with her head lowered and her face bright red. Hearing someone trash an author right in front of that author was quite a new experience.

After hesitating for a long time, Asuka Ren bowed her head and said,

“I'm sorry.”

Only then did Han Sooyoung seem to catch on.

“Wait, don't tell me······?”

Asuka Ren slowly nodded.

“······[Peace Land] is a setting I created.”

●

Perhaps Asuka Ren shouldn't have said that.

At first, Han Sooyoung couldn't contain her astonishment, saying things like, “Is that really true?” Five minutes later, she muttered, “Well, my novel became reality, too, so I guess it's possible.” Another five minutes later, she began outright bombarding Asuka Ren.

“Why did you do it?”

“······”

“Huh? I asked why you did it. Give me an answer, Miss Author. Why did you make the world so lousy?”

After being harangued for quite a while, Ren finally spoke, half in tears.

“Well······everything in Japan is isekai. So······”

“Aha, so you made this crap to rebel against mainstream isekai?”

“B-but as an author, I couldn't just churn out those formulaic stories.”

“Formuuulaic?”

It seemed she'd said something she shouldn't have.

“Your work is worse than formulaic crap, you idiot.”

“······What?”

After glaring at Asuka Ren as though she was pathetic, Han Sooyoung said to me,

“Hey, Kim Dokja. You know what? I learned something while I was in Veronica for a few days. In this world, counts use informal speech with dukes. And every last one of the so-called knights looks like some effeminate pretty boy, and all they know how to do is flop around······”

“W-wait a moment!”

“Shut up. We're going through all this trouble because of you.”

“······Yes, I created it, but I'm not the one who brought you here, you know?”

“Would you look at this bitch? You put the dokkaebis up to it and asked them to make your world real! Fuck, your manga flopped anyway! Let's shove all the bastards who trashed my manga into my setting and kill them all! You prayed for something like that, and suddenly, ta-da, you got some message saying, ‘I shall grant your wish.’ Right?”

I'd never heard such a creative theory before.

Maybe it really did take a special kind of person to be an author.

“N-no! There's no way something like that could be possible in the first place!”

“Then what was it?”

As I listened, I grew curious, too.

Even ‘Ways of Survival’ never explained why Asuka Ren's [Peace Land] had been chosen as a scenario.

If I learned how it had happened, might I also find a clue about the author of ‘Ways of Survival’?

“Well······”

That was when Han Sooyoung and I drew our swords at the same time.

Asuka Ren gave a startled hiccup and took a step back.

I said,

“I really do want to know, but it looks like now isn't a good time to hear it.”

“What?”

“Run!”

An instant later, several sharp shuriken embedded themselves where we'd been standing.

Only then did Asuka Ren desperately run after us, her face pale.

Han Sooyoung said,

“Fuck, when did they start following us?”

“They're good at stealth.”

“How many?”

“Four.”

Even with skills like theirs, they hadn't underestimated us; they'd tried to assassinate us.

We had no chance in a direct fight.

Asuka Ren spoke between gasps.

“I think they're the Wind Shadow Squad (風影隊). They're subordinates of the ‘Sovereign of Eight Heads.’”

“Those islanders sure know how to come up with flashy names.”

They shouldn't have been coming after us this soon. Apparently, mentioning Orochi's true name earlier had been a mistake.

Once we entered the rock formations, we had a little more room to maneuver.

Asuka Ren's guidance was proving its worth.

The author who created the setting really was in a class of her own.

Even so, the gap kept narrowing, and before long, the Wind Shadow Squad was right on our heels.

As though she'd made up her mind, Han Sooyoung said,

“Ah, forget it. Kim Dokja, go ahead. I'll buy you some time.”

“Will you be okay?”

“You know me, right? I'm a master at playing dead.”

“Then I'm counting on you.”

I grabbed Asuka Ren and ran.

“Ren-ssi, we really don't have any time now. We have to find that person quickly.”

“I-I don't know what you mean.”

“The returnee Kyrgios.”

“What?”

I spoke while deflecting an incoming shuriken.

It seemed Han Sooyoung had let a few of them slip past.

“Please tell me where Kyrgios is.”

“······I don't know who that is.”

I'd expected her to respond like this.

‘Ways of Survival’ only mentioned that Kyrgios was here at this point in time; there had never been a scene of anyone actually meeting him.

“No, you do know.”

“I really don't! I've never created a character like that!”

Asuka Ren cried out desperately.

“There's no one like that in my manga! Besides, all the characters in my manga are weak!”

“No.”

“What?”

Whooosh!

A shuriken finally flew past us and embedded itself ahead.

I swerved sharply and stopped.

Damn it, would I have to fight after all?

“Your [Peace Land] ended early, at installment 11, and as a result, it never even got a collected volume.”

“H-how do you know that······?”

“I understand that you wanted to draw traditional fantasy. But your manga isn't really ‘traditional fantasy,’ is it?”

Whoooosh.

Two members of the Wind Shadow Squad appeared in the smoke.

Normally, I would have been more than capable of handling them, but now, even holding off one was a struggle.

Baaang!

I'd only brushed a katana aside, but my wrist ached as though it would break.

I calmly activated ‘Blade of Faith’ and shouted,

“It only happened once during the serialization, but after checking your readers' reactions, you drew a certain character into the story in a fit of anger.”

“······W-what are you talking about?”

“That character was far too powerful for [Peace Land]. You felt guilty for adding a character like that to pander to the public. And that guilt ruined your [Peace Land].”

“No! I never did that!”

“Take responsibility to the very end. If even a single reader has followed this world······!”

“Ah, aaah······”

Dodging the blades was growing harder and harder.

Asuka Ren was completely frozen, perhaps in a panic.

Two katanas flew at me, aimed at my upper and lower body.

Damn it, had I been wrong?

“······I'm sorry. I'm so sorry.”

Then a voice reached me.

“You're right. I did, indeed······”

The next moment, the air around us changed.

A sudden chill ran down my spine, and I felt my limbs go rigid.

The voice that followed.

[Who are you?]

I didn't dare turn around, but there was no doubt that a being on par with a constellation was there. Otherwise, the [Fourth Wall] would never have shaken so violently.

Looking ahead, I saw that the Japanese men who had been thrusting their blades at me had also frozen like statues. White Pure (白淸) lightning struck from the sky at them as they stood unable even to speak.

Sssssss.

Those powerful disasters turned to dust and vanished beneath just two bolts of lightning.

Where the thunderclouds had disappeared, a small figure hovered.

It was unbelievable.

Because that proud, aloof fighter floating in the air was unmistakably a small person (小人).

······I'd found the right person.

[I will ask again. Who are you?]

“It's a pleasure to meet you, Kyrgios.”

Kyrgios Rodgraim, from [Peace Land].

He was one of the strongest returnees in Ways of Survival.

‘Constellations’ were commonly considered the strongest beings in the <Star Stream>.

Those who voyeuristically watched the world from the pinnacle of every story.

But as I'd said before, constellations weren't the only beings capable of opposing constellations.

There were demon kings who had rejected the path to a constellation's Status despite being capable of attaining it, rising instead to the pinnacle of demonic power. There were also dragons (龍) who reigned at the pinnacle of monster species from birth.

Then what about humans?

Could humans, who walked neither the demonic nor the nonhuman path, truly attain a Status capable of opposing constellations?

The answer to that question was right before my eyes.

[Interesting. Someone who gave up his own existence for another planet?]

Kyrgios seemed to have seen through even my identity with a single glance.

Looking at Asuka Ren, who had fainted beside me, he said,

[In recognition of that courage, I will let you off once. Take that woman and get out.]

Returnees.

Those born with exceptional talent who transcended humanity under the blessings of the <Star Stream>.

Even among them, Kyrgios Rodgraim was special.

A returnee who had gained exceptional power and attained a Status that kept him from being pulled into the gravity (引力) of the stories the dokkaebis created.

There were fewer than ten such returnees in all of ‘Ways of Survival’.

“I have something to tell you.”

[······Something to say?]

Skills that had attained transcendent Status bloomed all at once, making their presence known to me.

A being on the level of a constellation could destroy a mortal through its mere existence.

[Do you think you are in a position to speak to me?]

My back was instantly drenched in so much sweat that I was astonished my body held that much water.

[You dare address me, The Paradox (逆說) Baekchung (白淸)?]

He was strong.

The fact that a mortal—a small person, at that—could become so powerful gave me goosebumps.

[The exclusive skill ‘Fourth Wall’ activates!]

But I had a ‘wall.’ No matter how terrifying the being on the other side, he couldn't harm me as long as he couldn't cross it.

[The character, ‘Kyrgios Rodgraim,’ shows curiosity about you.]

By then, Kyrgios seemed to have noticed something strange, too.

[······You endured it? How? Are you under the protection of another being with high Status?]

I spoke before his curiosity could take an unwelcome turn.

“Kyrgios. This world needs your help.”

Kyrgios's expression changed oddly.

[Is that why you sought me out?]

“Yes.”

[That little fellow said the same thing······.]

Then that ‘little fellow’ responded.

[The small constellation of a small planet looks at ‘Kyrgios Rodgraim’ with tears in its eyes.]

[The small constellation of a small planet has sponsored ‘Kyrgios Rodgraim’ with 10 coins.]

Kyrgios frowned in apparent irritation.

[I have no need of it.]

[The small constellation of a small planet is deeply shocked.]

A few raindrops dribbled down from the sky like a baby's pee.

[······Every world has its time of ruin, and every story has a moment when it ends. For this planet, that time is now.]

There was no emotion in Kyrgios's eyes as he gazed into the distance.

But I knew. Even if someone grew numb to everything in the world, no being could escape the bonds of the ‘story’ they had built.

“Then why did you come back here? You left [Peace Land] long ago.”

[······Something called me.]

Kyrgios and I looked toward the fallen ‘Asuka Ren.’

I thought I might know what it was that Kyrgios felt.

“Don't lie to yourself. Didn't you return here to protect your home?”

[I have no fond memories of this place. This place is······.]

“The place that brought you into the world ‘weak’?”

For the first time, Kyrgios's gaze wavered.

“Is it because this is the damned home planet (母星) that gifted you that cursed body?”

[····You know a great deal about me for a mere incarnation of the scenarios. I will tell you one last time. Get out. There will be no third······.]

“Are you afraid?”

[What did you say?]

“I asked if you were afraid. Afraid of those constellations who have come here to ravage your world, of that wicked ‘snake.’ I asked······”

Rrrrrumble!

For a moment, the pressure crushing my entire body almost made my eyes pop out.

[If you wish to die, I will kill you.]

Even as I gasped for breath, I kept speaking.

“Don't lie about why you came here.”

[The constellation, ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband,’ disapproves of the conduct of ‘ Kyrgios Rodgraim’.]

[The constellation, ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire,’ rebukes the sense of justice of ‘Kyrgios Rodgraim’.]

[The constellation, ‘Scribe of Heaven,’ sternly condemns the interference in the scenario by ‘Kyrgios Rodgraim’.]

As the indirect messages appeared one after another, Kyrgios's oppressive presence briefly eased.

[Some peculiar beings follow at your heels. The Monkey King, and even archangels? How strange. Those prideful creatures······.]

Spitting out the blood pooled on my lips, I spoke again.

“Please focus on what I'm saying. Didn't you come to witness this planet's end?”

[I cannot help this planet.]

Bzzzt.

Blue sparks flew from his body.

A probability backlash.

It was the consequence of killing those two Wind Shadow Squad members earlier.

Since he hadn't been summoned to meet the scenario's needs, he was subject to some probability restrictions, though not as much as the constellations in the sky.

Kyrgios closed his fist tightly around the sparks leaping over his hand and said,

[If I bear the cost in probability and make the first move, I will only hasten this planet's destruction.]

I understood what he meant.

For beings on the level of constellations, probability was like a set of scales.

If one side changed the course of the story without valid grounds (介然), the laws of the <Star Stream> would forcibly try to balance those scales.

[If I interfere in the scenario, the other constellations watching it will also gain grounds to act. So all I can do······is carry the memory of my home's final moments with me.]

I remembered.

This was the true face of the ‘Kyrgios Rodgraim’ I knew.

Someone who had left home, overcome countless trials, and returned, only to find that the price of becoming too powerful was being unable to save his home.

That was The Paradox (逆說) Baekchung (白淸), Kyrgios Rodgraim.

“You don't need to act yourself.”

But if I were going to back down here, I would never have come to meet Kyrgios.

“By now, the heavenly order (天機) must be starting to demand a Story about a disciple from you. Isn't it?”

Even the composed Kyrgios looked deeply flustered this time.

“Take me as your disciple. I will act as your representative and defeat the disasters of [Peace Land].”

But his discomposure lasted only a moment.

[······I do not accept outsiders (外人) as disciples. And you lack the qualifications to inherit my power.]

That hurt my pride a little.

If it had been Yoo Joonghyuk standing here instead of me, would Kyrgios have accepted me as his disciple without hesitation?

“Would this be enough to qualify me?”

I picked up a nearby branch.

Whiiiine!

The magic power of [White Pure Star Energy] was drawn out in full, and vivid blue waves of magic surged at the tip of my blade. Its power was still lacking, but it was enough to demonstrate my attainment.

Kyrgios's eyes slowly filled with astonishment.

The hidden skill I'd purchased before anything else as soon as the second scenario ended.

White Pure Star Energy (白淸罡氣) was Kyrgios Rodgraim's signature technique.

“Allow me to greet you again. Kim Dokja, an outside (門外) disciple of the White Purity Sect (白淸門), pays his respects to an elder of his sect.”

.

.

Kyrgios made his decision some two hours later.

Releasing the White Pure energy that had blazed all over his body, he spoke in an ordinary human voice.

“The White Purity Sect should have been wiped out after I left. I never expected any disciples to remain.”

He'd kept me standing there for two whole hours just to say that.

They said the powerful beings of the Star Stream lived in their own ‘proper time’ to maintain their sense of self through the long ages. Perhaps that was true.

“Very well. I will accept you as my disciple.”

Kyrgios didn't ask how I'd learned White Pure Star Energy or how I knew his secret history.

And the training began.

●

「······Kyrgios Rodgraim was a ‘returnee from Murim.’

Despite the inherent limitations of being a ‘small person,’ his unparalleled efforts allowed him to master martial arts without the system's help and successfully transcend his species.

Many legends remain of him entering the <First Murim> and reigning as an absolute master. How he killed every Demonic Cult member taller than himself, how he cut off the penis of an alliance leader who mocked his height—among them, the most famous concerns his connection with the constellation ‘Snake Cutter’······.」

“······Your smartphone shrank with you?”

Hearing Han Sooyoung's voice as she approached, I turned off my smartphone and stood up.

“It ended up like this because I put it in my subspace coat.”

“Damn it, you always keep all the good stuff to yourself.”

The grumbling Han Sooyoung had safely shaken off the Wind Shadow Squad and managed to rejoin us. According to her, ‘playing dead’ had worked as usual. Since I'd fallen for it myself before, I thought that was plausible.

“I never imagined that ‘Kyrgios,’ the strongest in the <First Murim>, was from Peace Land.”

“The strongest hasn't been decided, but he's the closest to it. So you knew about him?”

“His name appears in the early part, too. This is my first time seeing him in person, though.”

“It's my first time, too. Anyway, take Ren and wait nearby.”

Under Kyrgios's instruction, I was learning his martial arts within a formation among the strange rocks.

My goal was to learn Kyrgios's secret technique within two weeks, then return to ‘Veronica Royal Castle.’

If events followed the original story, that would also be around the time Japan's king, the ‘Sovereign of Eight Heads,’ moved to trample all four royal castles.

Of course, there was no way things would work out as easily as I'd expected.

On the first day he began teaching me, Kyrgios instructed me to do the following.

“Do this a million times.”

“······A million times?”

“Yes, a million times. You got a good look at what I just showed you, didn't you?”

I had watched it.

Kyrgios had stood before me in a composed stance, then extended his sword and thrust it into the air. It was a basic ‘thrusting’ stance.

“Why do I have to······”

“All the martial arts of White Purity begin here. Opening the ‘smallest point.’ From a single, extremely condensed and restrained ‘point,’ the universe begins.”

“······I see.”

I had no idea what he meant.

“Beings born into a large race like yours wouldn't know what ‘smallness’ means.”

Something suddenly came to mind when I heard that.

According to the character background in ‘Ways of Survival’, Kyrgios had a complex about his height.

“Humans aren't particularly large, either.”

“Yes, that's exactly what I'm trying to say. From a cosmic perspective, every being amounts to less than a speck of dust. Thus, it is wrong to call small people small people. Humans and small people are ultimately nothing but dust.”

Somehow, it felt like he was justifying his own ‘smallness’ on a cosmic scale.

“But aren't large specks of dust different from small ones?”

“What matters is not the size of the dust, but the size of the universe. Even a being that amounts to a mere speck can have a different Status depending on how vast a universe it perceives. No, in fact, the smaller it is, the closer it is to the origin (根源) of the universe, so in fact it has an advantage in understanding the essence of things.”

It sounded impressive, so I went along with it for the moment.

“Aha.”

“Do you understand?”

“But what does that have to do with thrusting?”

Kyrgios gave me a contemptuous look and said,

“······This is why those born large are no good. Just work hard at your thrusts.”

With those words, Kyrgios disappeared.

He seemed disappointed in me.

Understandably.

My abysmal talent had already been amply demonstrated with [Way of the Wind]. If I actually tried to learn martial arts, two weeks would be out of the question; who knew how many decades it might take.

Four days passed after that.

“Do it properly. If you're inferior by birth, shouldn't you at least put in a proper effort?”

Another five days passed, and

“This is why those born with large bodies······”

A week had passed.

Still, Kyrgios's hatred of large people (大人) showed no sign of stopping.

“Why weren't you born an insect instead? Even a cockroach would probably learn better than you.”

“If there's a cockroach like that, I'd like to take it as my master.”

“Do you want to die?”

And finally, one evening in the second week.

I collapsed from exhaustion while practicing thrusts.

“You······”

I still hadn't learned the skill.

Deeply disappointed in my talent, Kyrgios gave me a look of disgust, then vanished. He seemed to have gone out for a little fresh air.

After making sure Kyrgios was completely gone, I sought out Asuka Ren and Han Sooyoung, who had been waiting nearby.

“Let's run away.”

“What? You've learned it all? You couldn't do a thing when I watched you earlier.”

“I've stolen it all.”

I quietly closed my eyes and murmured something. The next moment, fierce White Pure lightning leaped around me, and energy began to boil up.

It was Kyrgios's secret technique, [Electrification (電人化)].

“Huh? What's that? Just a moment ago, you definitely······”

“I told you. I stole it.”

[‘Kyrgios Rodgraim’ has been added to Bookmark slot 5.]

This had been my aim from the start.

To add Kyrgios, the strongest returnee, to my [Bookmark] and raise my understanding of him as much as possible.

Kyrgios probably hadn't intended to teach me properly in the first place.

Powerful beings like Kyrgios weren't so easily taken in that they'd hand over their ultimate techniques after a few honeyed words from me.

His aim was probably just to keep me here until the scenario ended, then torture me to extract the information I knew.

“So we need to run away quickly.”

“Damn it, fine.”

As Han Sooyoung grumbled and finished getting ready, I saw the sun beginning to rise in the distance.

The warmth of dawn was spreading over our surroundings.

In [Peace Land], the seasons changed once every two weeks.

It had definitely been winter when I started training, but now spring was coming.

That was when Asuka Ren's face went pale.

“······The ‘Sovereign of Eight Heads’ has begun to move.”

“Are you sure?”

“I can hear him calling the Japanese people through the [Absolute Throne].”

I'd thought it was about time.

Spring, when the creatures that had settled into hibernation woke one by one.

At last, the season for ‘snake hunting’ had arrived.

Veronica's high battlements. From those heights, giants could be seen filling the plains below. Beings who had once been human, but were now disasters. Activating every turret of his fortress, Gong Pildu roared,

“You goddamn bastards. This is my land!”

The Japanese people charging across the plains, smashing them apart, numbered a staggering fifty.

There was no way to know for sure, but a force that size probably represented at least half the disasters in [Peace Land].

Ratatatat!

“Get lost―!”

Gong Pildu was a little unhinged as he fired his cannons.

Why he had ended up that way was unknown.

But Lee Jihye had a thought.

Perhaps he was still suffering the aftereffects of having his ‘Green Zone’ destroyed by Kim Dokja.

Lee Jihye's fingertips trembled as she watched the vast army of disasters surge toward them.
